title: Perfect completeness and soundness for odd weight
statement: For every natural number $m$, the Boolean proof oracle on $m$ positions obtained by omitting the final, fixed true bit from the partial-sum verifier is a probabilistically checkable proof system for Boolean strings of length $m+2$ having odd parity, with rate $1$. Thus every odd-parity input has some proof accepted with probability $1$, and for every $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, every input whose relative Hamming distance from each odd-parity string is greater than $\varepsilon$ is rejected with probability strictly greater than $\varepsilon$, for every proof.
hypotheses_covered: the input is Boolean of length $m+2$
the proof is Boolean of length $m$
the input is at relative Hamming distance greater than $\varepsilon$ from every odd-parity string
